questions.prompt: A software pattern is best described as:

options.text: A reusable solution to a known problem in a well-defined context
A finished library you can import

questions.explanation: A pattern is a reusable solution to a known problem within a well-defined context, defined by context, problem (forces), and solution.

questions.prompt: In the GoF classification, which category does the Singleton pattern belong to?
questions.explanation: Singleton is a creational pattern, alongside Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype, and Factory Method.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are GoF structural patterns?
questions.explanation: Adapter, Decorator, and Facade are structural patterns; Observer is behavioral.

questions.prompt: Which pattern embeds each behavioral variation inside an object passed as a parameter to an algorithm?
questions.explanation: Strategy embeds each variation in a strategy object implementing a common interface, passed to the algorithm (e.g. java.util.Comparator).

questions.prompt: The Template Method pattern defines the stable core of an algorithm and lets subclasses provide variations at specific points via abstract primitive operations.
questions.explanation: Template Method keeps a stable algorithm core that invokes abstract primitive operations overridden by subclasses (e.g. the Sorter/StringSorter example).

questions.prompt: Which Proxy variant creates expensive objects only on demand?
questions.explanation: A virtual proxy creates expensive objects on demand (e.g. slow-loading resources); a remote proxy is a local representative for an object in another address space.

questions.prompt: In the MVC pattern, which part should remain as separate as possible from the user interface?
questions.explanation: Application logic (the Model) must remain as separate as possible from the user interface (View = layout, Controller = events).

questions.prompt: Inheritance and composition are both ways to achieve reuse, but composition delegates requests to an included object.
questions.explanation: With inheritance the reusing class inherits methods directly; with composition it holds an included object and delegates client requests to it.

questions.prompt: Which type of pattern expresses a fundamental structural organization schema for entire software systems?
questions.explanation: Architectural patterns address system-wide structures; design patterns refine components; idioms are language-specific low-level patterns.

questions.prompt: Which pattern lets a class with an unexpected interface be integrated without modifying its source?
questions.explanation: Adapter integrates a provider class whose interface is not the one expected, without modifying it; it is the only structural pattern where inheritance plays the key role.

questions.prompt: Which pattern represents part-whole hierarchies so clients treat individual and composed objects uniformly?
questions.explanation: Composite represents part-whole hierarchies (e.g. Java Swing JPanel containment) so clients can treat individual and composite objects the same way.

questions.prompt: The Decorator pattern adds responsibilities to individual objects dynamically without an explosion of subclasses.
questions.explanation: Decorator extends an object's behaviour dynamically without subclass explosion; Java's JScrollPane and BufferedReader are examples.

questions.prompt: Which pattern provides an object to traverse a collection without exposing its internal storage?
questions.explanation: Iterator provides an iterator object attached to the collection, allowing multiple concurrent iterations without exposing internal storage (java.util.Iterator).

questions.prompt: Which pattern supports very large numbers of fine-grained objects efficiently by sharing intrinsic state?
questions.explanation: Flyweight shares common (intrinsic) state across many fine-grained objects to save memory; Java's Integer pooling is an example.

questions.prompt: Which are listed consequences of the Observer pattern?

options.text: Abstract coupling between Subject and Observer
Guaranteed compile-time type safety of updates

questions.explanation: Observer gives abstract coupling and broadcast support (pros) but risks unanticipated updates (con).

questions.prompt: A fluent interface uses extensive method chaining to improve readability, often forming a domain-specific language.
questions.explanation: Fluent interfaces rely on method chaining to read like prose and create a DSL-like API; Java Stream and Optional are examples.

questions.prompt: Which creational pattern is used when a complex object must be created through a complex, step-by-step interaction, with different variations possible?
questions.explanation: Builder is used when creating a complex object entails complex interaction and different variations of the target object might be produced (often with a fluent builder).

questions.prompt: What problem does the Abstract Factory pattern address?

options.text: A client should not know which variant of a family of related classes it is creating/using
An object needs exactly one instance
An interface is not the one expected by a client
Behaviour must be added to objects dynamically

questions.explanation: Abstract Factory handles a family of related classes with different implementations so the client doesn't know which variant it is creating or using.

questions.prompt: Which are consequences of the Visitor pattern?

options.text: Adding new operations is very easy
It can visit class hierarchies and accumulate state
Adding new concrete elements is difficult

questions.explanation: Visitor makes adding operations easy, can visit hierarchies and accumulate state, but makes adding new concrete elements difficult and breaks encapsulation.

questions.prompt: What characterizes duck typing in a dynamically typed language?

options.text: You just add a method to a class and can call it, with no compile-time type checking
You must define interfaces and classes before calling a method
All types are checked at compile time
Methods cannot be added after class definition

questions.explanation: With duck typing you simply add a method and call it — no interfaces or compile-time type checking, unlike strongly typed languages.

questions.prompt: Following the Java Bean convention, how are accessors for a property 'Prop' defined?

options.text: Getter getProp() and (optional) setter setProp(T value)
Only a public field named prop
A method prop() returning a map
An interface HasProp with no methods

questions.explanation: The Java Bean convention defines a getter getProp() and an optional setter setProp(T value) for a property Prop.

questions.prompt: Which pattern creates objects from a palette of similar classes to avoid a complex class hierarchy differentiated by minor parameters?
questions.explanation: Prototype creates objects from a palette of similar classes, avoiding a complex hierarchy whose classes differ only by minor parameters.

questions.prompt: Which pattern does this Java code from the slides implement?
questions.explanation: A private constructor plus a static getInstance() that lazily creates the single instance is the Singleton pattern. Source: SwD&A Design Patterns slides (Marco Torchiano) — 'Singleton class' example.

questions.prompt: Which design pattern is illustrated by Comparator in this slide example?
questions.explanation: Passing a java.util.Comparator to Arrays.sort embeds the comparison variation in a strategy object — the Strategy pattern. Source: SwD&A Design Patterns slides — 'Strategy example: Comparator'.

questions.prompt: Which pattern keeps the stable sort algorithm fixed while letting subclasses define compare()?
questions.explanation: Sorter defines the algorithm core and calls the abstract primitive compare(), which a subclass like StringSorter overrides — the Template Method pattern. Source: SwD&A Design Patterns slides — 'Example: Sorter / StringSorter'.

questions.prompt: Which idiom does this object-construction code from the slides demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Extensive method chaining that reads like prose to build a complex object is a fluent interface (DSL-like). Source: SwD&A Design Patterns slides — 'Fluent builder' example (Measure).

questions.prompt: Which patterns underlie the structure and evaluation of this expression tree from the slides?
questions.code:
Expression e = new Operation('*', new Value(6), new Operation('+', new Value(4), new Value(3)));
IO.println(e.formula() + " = " + e.eval());

options.text: Composite (operators and operands form a tree)

questions.explanation: The Abstract Syntax Tree uses Composite for operators/operands, and evaluation uses the Interpreter and Visitor patterns. Source: SwD&A Design Patterns slides — 'Abstract Syntax Tree / Expression Tree' example.
